summary: Carola Roloff is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied under Geshe Thubten Ngawang and David P. Jackson, earning her Dr. phil. from the University of Hamburg (1997–2009). She has held appointments at Hamburg, CIHTS, and Oslo.

Carola S. Carstens is a scholar in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies who earned her Doktor der Philosophie from the University of Hamburg by 2006. She held a post at Rice University from 1998 to 1999.
Carole M. Cusack is a religious studies scholar who earned her PhD from the University of Sydney (1988–1995). In 2013, she served as Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Sydney.

Carole McGranahan is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. After studying at Colgate University and earning her PhD at the University of Michigan (1993–2001), she served as Assistant Professor of Anthropology at the University of Colorado Boulder (~2001–2008).

Caroline Humphrey is a scholar of religious studies and Iranian/Central Asian studies who completed degrees at Leeds and Cambridge, studying under Edmund Leach. Her career included posts at Girton College and serving as a Hochschullehrerin at Cambridge (1978–2010).

Caroline Rhys Davids worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. Educated at University College London, she was General Editor of the Pali Text Society (1907–1942) and lectured at the University of Manchester (1910–1913) and SOAS (1918–1933).

Carolyn Woodford Schmidt is an archaeologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned doctorates from Ohio State University and Wichita State University. She held posts at Ohio State, Denison University, and served as Director at the University of Kansas in 2017.
Carson T. Schütze is a linguist who studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology from 1992 to 1997. In 1997, he held a post at the University of California, Los Angeles.

Carsten Colpe was a scholar of religious studies and Iranian/Central Asian studies who studied under Hans Heinrich Schaeder (~1950–1954). He held academic posts at the University of Göttingen (~1956–1969) and the Free University of Berlin (~1969–1997).

Caterina Conio was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied at Catholic University of the Sacred Heart, Banaras Hindu University, and Florence under T. R. V. Murti and Paul Hacker. In 1974, she taught at the University of Pisa.
Catharine Bird Runkle was an Indology scholar who studied at Radcliffe College in 1886 and was taught by Charles Rockwell Lanman.

Catherine Bell was a scholar of religious studies and sinology who studied at the University of Chicago under Joseph M. Kitagawa (~1976–1983). From 1985 to 2008, she was Bernard J. Hanley Professor at Santa Clara University.

Catherine Cornille is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who earned degrees from KU Leuven and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa. She held posts at KU Leuven, College of the Holy Cross, and Boston College.

Catherine Ella Blanshard Asher was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who earned her PhD at the University of Minnesota Twin Cities (~1972–1984), where she also served as Assistant Professor from ~1985 to 2021.

Catherine Ludvik is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology who earned her PhD from the University of Toronto. She has held posts at the Italian School of East Asian Studies, Doshisha, Kyoto Sangyo, Stanford, and Hanazono.

Catherine Prueitt is a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and religious studies who earned her PhD at Emory University under John D. Dunne. She was an assistant professor at George Mason University (2017–2019) before joining the University of British Columbia (2019).
Cathy Cantwell is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD from the University of Kent (~1984–1989). In 2002, she held a post at the University of Oxford.

Cecil Bendall was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar educated at Cambridge and Göttingen. He held posts at the British Museum, University College London as Professor of Sanskrit (1885–1903), and the University of Cambridge as Professor (1900–1906).

Cecil Henry Bompas was an Indology scholar who studied at Trinity College, Cambridge (1886–1889). He served in the Indian Civil Service (1887–1923), the Bengal Legislative Council (1916), and chaired the Calcutta Improvement Trust (1920).

Cecil Jermyn Brown was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who earned an M.A. from Trinity College, Oxford. He taught at Canning College (1909–1920) and was later Professor of English Literature at the University of Lucknow (1923–1926).
